title: Animal sorting cards
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Skeletons, muscles, nutrition and plants (Tribal Tales)
source: Seeded from science/y3 lesson 19 (Animal sorting cards (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 19: Vertebrates and invertebrates. To understand how animals can be sorted by whether they have a backbone

blocks.title: Sort into: Vertebrate / Invertebrate
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Vertebrate, Invertebrate.
blocks.answer: Vertebrate: Cat; Eagle; Frog; Salmon; Lizard. Invertebrate: Worm; Spider; Snail; Ant; Crab

questions.q: Is a frog a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
questions.model: Ask one question: does it have a backbone? A frog has a spine inside, so it is a vertebrate.

questions.q: Is a slug a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
Name a vertebrate that lives in water.
questions.a: For example: a fish or a dolphin

questions.q: Sort ten animal picture cards on the sheet into two columns: vertebrate and invertebrate.
questions.a: Vertebrates: cat, eagle, frog, salmon, lizard. Invertebrates: worm, spider, snail, ant, crab
questions.model: Teacher sorts the cat first: 'A cat has a backbone, so it goes under vertebrate.'

questions.q: Look in a garden, park or window box with an adult. List two invertebrates you could find there.
questions.a: For example: woodlouse, ant, spider, snail, worm

questions.q: How does an exoskeleton help a beetle? Give one good thing and one problem.
questions.a: Good: protects and supports it. Problem: it cannot grow, so it must moult.

questions.q: A vertebrate is an animal with...
Big question: what is the big difference inside a worm and a snake?
questions.a: The snake has a backbone; the worm does not.
